newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rate up to 11.2 pct on high demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rate up to 11.2 pct on high demand.

text.p: High demand and a modest suply of kuna funds lifted the Croatian average lending rate to 11.2 percent on Monday from 10.9 percent, dealers said.
They put daily settlements at 40.1 million kuna, though there was demand for another 60 million.
Fresh loans accounted for 29.5 million kuna, mostly call money loans granted at a steady 10.5 percent, with one loan struck at 15 percent.
Insurers extended previous one-week funds at a steady nine percent and banks charged 16-18 percent for old one-month and two month loans.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday firmer at 6.0523 against the dollar and weaker at 3.5802 against the German mark. --Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
